5

18	`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.
19	
20	---
21	
22	*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
23	from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*
24	
25	## OfficeFloor REST endpoints
26	
27	Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
28	OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
29	pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.
30	
31	- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
32	  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
33	  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
34	  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
35	- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
36	  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
37	- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
38	- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
39	- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
40	- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.
41	
42	### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`
43	
44	The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.
45	
46	`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`
47	
48	```yaml
49	# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
50	# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
51	validate:
52	  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
53	  next: load
54	load:
55	  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
56	  next: apply
57	apply:
58	  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
59	  govern: [ transaction ]
60	  next: save
61	save:
62	  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
63	  govern: [ transaction ]
64	  next: respond
65	respond:
66	  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
67	```
68	
69	```java
70	// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
71	public class ValidateOwner {
72	  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
73	    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
74	  }
75	}
76	public class LoadOwner {
77	  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
78	      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
79	    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
80	    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
81	    ownerOut.set(owner);
82	  }
83	}
84	public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
85	  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
86	    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
87	    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
88	  }
89	}
90	public class SaveOwner {
91	  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
92	    repository.save(owner);
93	  }
94	}
95	public class RespondWithOwner {
96	  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
97	    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
98	  }
99	}
100	```
101	
102	`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`
103	
104	```yaml
105	handle:
106	  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
107	```
108	
109	```java
110	public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
111	  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
112	      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
113	    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
114	  }
115	}
116	```
117	
118	### Step wiring
119	
120	Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
121	point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
122	method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
123	`method:`.
124	
125	- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
126	  as `@Parameter T`.
127	- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
128	  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
129	  branch; not calling it short-circuits.
130	
131	### Function parameters
132	
133	Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:
134	
135	- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
136	- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
137	- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
138	  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
139	  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
140	- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
141	  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.
142	
143	### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`
144	
145	Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
146	into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):
147	
148	- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
149	- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
150	  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
151	- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
152	  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.
153	
154	### Naming
155	
156	Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
157	absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
158	publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
159	`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).
160	
161	Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
162	responder. Steps in between work with entities.
163	
164	### Request body and validation
165	
166	- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
167	  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
168	  first step publishes it as a variable.
169	- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
170	  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
171	  invalid body can return 400.
172	
173	### Transactions
174	
175	`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
176	listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
177	the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.
178	
179	### Errors
180	
181	Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
182	Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
183	`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
184	`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
185	anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.
186	
187	### Security
188	
189	Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:
190	
191	```yaml
192	composition:
193	  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
194	```
195	
196	- Full reference: https://officefloor.net/llms.txt

    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default

into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):

- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.

### Naming

Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).

Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
responder. Steps in between work with entities.

### Request body and validation

- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
  first step publishes it as a variable.
- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
  invalid body can return 400.

### Transactions

`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.

### Errors

Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.

### Security

Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:

```yaml
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
```

content.text:
Patrons and backing are working, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**How it works**
- Each person's row now has a patron dropdown and an "Add patron" button. The dropdown lists everyone else on the sheet, so a person can't pick themselves.
- The server refuses a person as their own patron, the same patron twice, or a patron who isn't on the sheet. A refusal shows an error on the row, saves nothing and writes nothing to the audit file. Choosing in the dropdown or pressing the button again clears the error.
- Each successful add writes `PATRON_ADDED sheet=… by=… name=<person> patron=<patron>` to the audit file.
- Two new columns on each row:
  - **Patrons:** the names, comma and space separated, sorted ignoring case.
  - **Backing:** the patrons' due-totals added up, skipping n/a, and 0.00 with no patrons. It's worked out on the screen from the same due-totals the rows already show, so it follows holds, rate changes and other changes to those totals.

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** a new `person_patron` table in migration `V20__person_patron.sql`.
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/patrons`, handled by `ValidatePatron` and `AddPatron`. Each person returned by the server now also carries `patrons` (sorted names) and `patronIds`.
- **Front end:** a new `PatronControl.tsx`, plus the two columns in `PeopleList.tsx`.

Retired people still appear in the patron dropdown. The request didn't say whether they should, so I left them in.
